A.explanation: A meson is a hadron made of a quark and an antiquark, so it is not a lepton.

B.explanation: A positron is the antiparticle of the electron and belongs to the lepton family, which are fundamental particles.

C.explanation: A proton is a baryon hadron made of three quarks ($uud$), so it is not a lepton.

D.explanation: A quark is a fundamental particle but belongs to the quark family, not the lepton family.

walkthrough: Identify the two main families to compare: leptons are fundamental particles like electrons and neutrinos, while hadrons like mesons and baryons are made of quarks.
Recall that a meson is a hadron consisting of one quark and one antiquark, so it belongs to the hadron group, not the lepton group.
Recall that a proton is a baryon hadron consisting of three quarks, so it also belongs to the hadron group, not the lepton group.
Recall that a quark is a separate fundamental family from leptons, so a quark itself cannot be a lepton.
The positron is the antiparticle of the electron with charge $+e$ and lepton number $-1$, and it is not made of quarks, so it fits the definition of a lepton. This is option B.
